With as much as Kenji gets into the scientific reasoning behind why things happen when cooking I'm surprised he's not a fan of cold searing. You build a sear a little at a time flipping more often on lower heat. No oil splatter, you actually don't even use oil just plop the steak in the pan, and next to zero grey banding. It lets the extreme heat out that would have otherwise given you that grey band between the sear and the pink center. Sous vide helps that but it's not as good as a cold sear. Start in a cold nonstick pan, turn to medium-high, no oil, flip at 2 minutes, flip again after 2 minutes, reduce to medium and keep flipping every minute or so until it temps at 125° 🤤🤤

For years I used reverse sear, and it often produced great results, but many times it did not. Too often I would remove from low heat at the right temp, only to overshoot during the sear. Other times, I would trying taking the meat off a little earlier, which sometimes resulted in undercooking. Bottom line -- every steak is a little different so the temps are much more critical when using reverse sear. Searing first lets me use the less predictable high heat at the beginning then put the steak in a low grill/oven/pan and slowly get up to the EXACT temp that I want. The sear first method (again, for me) is much more forgiving and much more consistent.

I don’t mind the flavor of charred pepper, but the reason I don’t season my steaks with anything but salt before searing is because it drastically improves the consistency of your sear.

With no seasoning that can burn, the surface of the steak is completely in contact with the pan. There’s 0 risk of seasoning getting stuck on the pan & leaving a big grey spot on your steak. This way you can also flip constantly, which is my preferred method for achieving a good sear.
